title: Once Default
statement: Implement `solve(captured, fresh)`. Both are integer timestamps. A default argument captured `captured` when the function was defined. A correct call reads `fresh` at call time. Return `{"stale": captured, "live": fresh, "same": 1 or 0}` where `same` is 1 when the two numbers are equal. The stale value is what a mutable or early-bound default would keep serving.
hints: Echo both numbers. Do not replace one with the other.
same is 1 only when they compare equal.
The point of the function is to show the captured value surviving a later fresh read.

approaches.name: Direct
approaches.explanation: Default expressions run once, at function definition.

editorial: Default expressions run once, at function definition. A timestamp default therefore freezes the first value. Reading the clock inside the body gets the live value. Returning both makes the staleness visible instead of hiding it behind a single number.
reference_solution:
def solve(captured, fresh):
    return {"stale": captured, "live": fresh, "same": 1 if captured == fresh else 0}
